motivation: Community-insurance v1 supports greater occupancy retention after exact-point Thalassia loss in pre-existing mixed-species patches. Test whether retaining another seagrass in the loss year is associated with greater one-year focal return, distinguishing habitat-state continuity from simple visual persistence.

primary_population.sequence: same stable point observed in years t, t+1, t+2; Thalassia present at t, absent at t+1; t+2 biological state observed

H4a_habitat_continuity_recovery.statement: After exact-point Thalassia loss, meter marks that remain occupied by another seagrass in the loss year have higher one-year Thalassia return probability than meter marks that become seagrass-bare.
H4a_habitat_continuity_recovery.outcome: Thalassia present at the same point in t+2
H4a_habitat_continuity_recovery.estimator: node-cluster bootstrap difference in one-year return fraction: vegetated loss-year point minus bare loss-year point
H4a_habitat_continuity_recovery.support_rule: bootstrap 95% interval for vegetated-minus-bare return difference entirely above zero

H4b_preexisting_insurance_recovery.statement: Among loss-year points occupied by another seagrass, points retaining at least one alternative species already present with Thalassia at t have higher one-year focal return than points occupied only by newly appearing alternatives.
H4b_preexisting_insurance_recovery.exposure: retained_preexisting_alternative versus new_only alternative occupancy at t+1
H4b_preexisting_insurance_recovery.estimator: node-cluster bootstrap difference in one-year return fraction: retained-preexisting minus new-only

descriptive_only: return fractions by loss-year alternative species identity
claim_boundary: Higher return from vegetated loss-year points would be consistent with habitat/community continuity but would not establish facilitation.
Return means recorded reappearance at the same sampled meter mark, not genet-level recolonization or demographic recovery.
Alternative species may be indicators of persistent favorable habitat rather than causal agents of focal return.
Do not change the pooled geography, one-year return horizon, loss definition, bootstrap unit, or support thresholds after opening t+2 focal states.
